question: Can standard Spin(10)-breaking branch projectors from 45_H or 210_H, combined with marked family projectors, generate the claim-1538 sector tensor Xi from one universal 126 Yukawa matrix?

boundedClass.branchSpace: B=B_D direct-sum B_M with orthogonal idempotents b_D,b_M
boundedClass.familySpace: F=P direct-sum I direct-sum N with commuting primitive projectors p_P,p_I,p_N
boundedClass.universalTensor: one symmetric Y in Sym2(F*) multiplying 16_F 16_F 126_H
boundedClass.allowedOperations: operator polynomials of degree at most two in commuting branch/family projectors, in the generous normal form allowing one projector insertion on each fermion leg
boundedClass.normalForm: Y_b=sum_(r<=s) c_(b,rs) [p_r Y p_s+p_s Y p_r]/(1+delta_rs), for b=D,M
boundedClass.cpSlice: all coefficients may be taken real; the complex count is otherwise identical

projectorAlgebraTheorem.idempotentReduction: Every polynomial in the commuting primitive projectors reduces to a diagonal linear combination of their joint spectral projectors.
projectorAlgebraTheorem.action: each basis coefficient Y_rs is independently retained, killed or rescaled in each branch
cannotDo: move Y_PP into the PN coordinate
equate two distinct universal Yukawa entries
projectorAlgebraTheorem.strongerBoundary: Raising polynomial degree does not help while all generators remain commuting projectors.

supportClassification.description: six independent symmetric family coordinates in each of the D and M branches
supportClassification.qualification: support reachability is not coefficient identification

coefficientFreedom.withIndependentWilsonCoefficients: alpha, beta, a and c are independent subject only to external assumptions
coefficientFreedom.withOneCommonWilsonCoefficient: setting alpha=beta=w still gives (k_D,k_M)=w(a,c), a two-dimensional family-entry image as Y varies
coefficientFreedom.requiredExtraEquation: c=kappa a, not generated by projector algebra

breakingProjectorAudit.roleOf45or210: A standard 45_H or 210_H breaking VEV can distinguish Pati-Salam subrepresentations and hence supply diagonal branch projectors b_D and b_M after choosing the vacuum.
breakingProjectorAudit.familyAction: these Spin(10)-breaking projectors are family blind
breakingProjectorAudit.result: they can keep different support masks in the D and M scalar branches but cannot change or relate the family matrix coordinates
breakingProjectorAudit.normalizationBoundary: their eigenvalue normalization and threshold factors may rescale alpha and beta, adding freedom rather than removing the a/c freedom

targetAttempt.polynomialMask: b_D tensor (p_P on both legs) plus b_M tensor sym(p_P,p_N)
targetAttempt.failure: a=Y_PP and c=Y_PN remain independent entries of the universal tensor; writing the two masks with equal displayed polynomial coefficients does not make a=c

minimumNewSpurion.noncommutativity: t_NP is off diagonal and is not contained in the commuting projector algebra
minimumNewSpurion.transport: for A=p_P Y p_P=a E_PP, t_NP A+A t_NP^T=a(E_NP+E_PN)
minimumNewSpurion.commonCoefficient: both branches now use the same universal entry a=Y_PP and one overall normalization
minimumNewSpurion.minimality: Any linear family operator producing a PN component from PP must have a nonzero P-to-N or N-to-P matrix element; rank one is the smallest possibility.

explicitConstructionOutsideBound.cost: one branch-conditioned rank-one family partial isometry, with its transpose/J partner and fixed normalization

candidateResults.reason: diagonal masks preserve a and c as independent entries
more branch eigenvalues do not create a family off-diagonal transporter
transports the single PP coefficient to PN only in the Majorana branch

strongestNoGo: In the degree-at-most-two commuting-projector class, even granting all primitive P/I/N family projectors and exact D/M branch projectors, the selected coefficient map has rank two: (a,c) maps to (alpha a,beta c). The target support is selectable, but a one-dimensional common ray is not. This remains true at any polynomial degree unless a noncommuting family operator or an external relation c=kappa a is added.
reopeningDatum: Derive a normalized branch-conditioned partial isometry t_NP, or an equivalent finite-geometry one-form/natural transformation, from the Spin(10)-broken theory. It must act only in the Majorana branch, include its J/CP partner, avoid the Dirac P-N support, and have its normalization and radiative stability fixed rather than supplied as another Wilson coefficient.
verdict: Standard 45_H or 210_H branch projectors can reproduce the desired zero pattern but cannot derive Xi's common coefficient from one universal 126 Yukawa tensor. The minimum additional datum is a rank-one off-diagonal P-to-N family partial isometry conditioned on the Majorana branch.
